bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Speech Pathology Salary

If you are a speech pathologist or considering the profession, knowing how your hourly rate translates into an annual salary is essential for budgeting, negotiating, and planning your career. This guide explains the award rates, the calculation method, and how tax and super affect your take-home pay.

### Award Rates for Speech Pathologists

Speech pathologists are typically covered by the **Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020**. Under this award, a Health Professional employee is classified by their qualification level and years of experience. For a newly qualified speech pathologist with a Bachelor degree (AQF Level 5) in their first year, the minimum hourly rate from 1 July 2026 is **$32.44 per hour**. With a four-year Honours degree (AQF Level 8), the rate is **$35.19 per hour**. These rates increase with experience and as you move to Level 2 and beyond.

It is important to note that these are minimum rates. Many employers pay above award, and enterprise agreements may set different rates. Always check your specific employment contract or agreement.

### Calculating Your Annual Speech Pathology Salary

The standard formula for converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time speech pathologist, the award defines ordinary hours as an average of **38 per week**. Using the Level 1 (AQF Level 5, 1st year) rate:

$32.44 × 38 × 52 = **$64,125.44 per year**

If you work part-time, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. For example, 30 hours per week would give $32.44 × 30 × 52 = $50,606.40.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your gross fortnightly pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For the full-time example above:

Weekly pay = $32.44 × 38 = $1,232.72
Fortnightly pay = $1,232.72 × 2 = **$2,465.44**

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual speech pathologist, you are entitled to a **25% loading** on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave or other entitlements. For the Level 1 rate:

$32.44 × 1.25 = **$40.55 per hour**

Annualising this at 38 hours per week gives $40.55 × 38 × 52 = **$80,126.80** before tax and super. Remember, casual hours may vary, so your actual annual income could differ.

### Tax on Your Speech Pathology Salary

Your gross annual salary is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates for residents in 2026–27:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, the **Medicare levy** of 2% generally applies. For a salary of $64,125, the tax (excluding Medicare) would be approximately:

- First $18,200: $0
- Next $26,800 (to $45,000): $4,020
- Remaining $19,125 (to $64,125): $5,737.50
- Total tax: $9,757.50
- Medicare levy (2%): $1,282.50
- Total deductions: **$11,040**
- Approximate take-home pay: **$53,085 per year**

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a more precise estimate.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Your employer must pay **superannuation guarantee** contributions of **12%** of your ordinary earnings on top of your salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per quarter. For the $64,125 salary, that is an extra $7,695 per year paid into your super fund. This amount is not included in your take-home pay but grows your retirement savings.

### Comparing with National Minimum Wage and Average Earnings

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a full-time employee, or $1,004.90 per week. A speech pathologist at $32.44 per hour earns about 23% above the minimum. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week (approx. $108,352 per year). A Level 1 speech pathologist's salary is below this average, but with experience and progression to Level 2 or higher, earnings can exceed the average.

### Using Our Timesheet

To quickly estimate your annual salary from your hourly rate, try our [timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate (do not include casual loading – check the casual loading box if applicable) and your weekly hours. The tool will calculate your gross annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, and show an estimate of tax and Medicare.

### Important Considerations

- The formula assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.
- Salary packaging or sacrifice arrangements are not included.
- The Medicare levy surcharge (for singles earning over $93,000 or families over $186,000) is not deducted here.
- HELP or HECS repayments are not included.

Always consult a qualified tax professional for your individual circumstances.

- [Super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) – understand super contributions
- [Average pay](/topics/average-pay) – compare with industry averages

### Summary

A speech pathology salary at the entry-level award rate is around $64,125 per year before tax. With casual loading, it rises to about $80,127. After tax and Medicare, take-home pay is roughly $53,085. Super adds another $7,695 to your retirement savings. As you gain experience and move up classification levels, your earnings will increase. Use the resources on this site to plan your finances with confidence.
